summary: Legacy CI: cross-cloud auth failures after org-policy and STS tag length enforcement
description:
Issue summary:
Legacy CI job (pipeline: infra-deploy/legacy-bootstrap) started failing to access resources across GCP and AWS after a policies rollout. The pipeline uses a hybrid auth path: a GCP service account key (historically long-lived) to trigger an internal service which then assumes an AWS role across accounts. Over the last 24 hours builds are failing at two distinct points: GCP SA key creation/usage is being rejected and the AWS AssumeRole step is returning AccessDenied with a message about session tag length.

Context:
- This pipeline is used by a small set of infra teams for experimental provisioning and cannot be migrated quickly to the new short-lived OIDC flow due to downstream tooling that expects a JSON key file.
- Security rolled out two org-level controls yesterday: GCP policy disableServiceAccountKeyCreation=true for new accounts, and an AWS STS tag length enforcement patch that truncates session tags longer than 128 chars.

Primary ask:
- Restore pipeline functionality for affected teams with minimal blast radius while we implement a longer-term migration to short-lived, auditable credentials.
impact: Multiple repo owners report failing deploys and blocked rollouts. Approx 7 pipelines per day impacted across prod us-east and eu-west. No customer-facing outages yet, but internal infra automation is degraded.
steps_to_reproduce: Trigger infra-deploy/legacy-bootstrap pipeline from GitHub Actions with a build id that contains long metadata (branch name + commit + feature flag metadata).
Pipeline attempts to load stored service-account.json from internal secrets bucket and calls GCP IAM API to sign a token for downstream service.
Observe GCP error: "PermissionDenied: Service account key creation is disabled by organization policy" when any job attempts to refresh the legacy key.

If key already exists, pipeline proceeds to call our internal broker which attempts to call AWS sts:AssumeRole with session tags assembled from build metadata and fails with AccessDenied and a message referencing session tag conditions or truncated tag length.
logs: gcp-iam-error: "PermissionDenied: createKey: Disabled by organization policy (projects/123456789/serviceAccounts/ci-legacy@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com)"

aws-sts-error: "User: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/infra-broker-role/ci-job is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource: arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/deploy-role because session tag length exceeded allowed size"
pipeline-run-id: build-20260310-87a33f; full-build-metadata-length: 214 chars; truncated-on-assume: true
investigation_notes: 03/10 11:22 - Triage: confirmed error reproduced using a manual run with identical metadata payload. (Elliot)
03/10 12:10 - Confirmed org policy disableServiceAccountKeyCreation is set at org level and applied to the project. (Security/Ops change window: 03/09 22:00)

03/10 12:45 - AWS backend change log review: enforcement of tag length checks rolled out to infra accounts on 03/09. Observed that our broker concatenates multiple metadata fields into a single tag payload exceeding new length limits.
03/10 13:30 - Verified that existing long-lived SA keys that predate policy still work unless rotated; new key creation attempts now fail. Workflows that try to rotate keys fail upfront.

03/11 09:00 - Reproduced AWS AssumeRole failure when session tags length > 128 chars. Shortening tag payload to 80 chars allows assume role to succeed. (SRE repro harness attached in related_github_prs)
hypotheses: Org policy prevents programmatic creation of new GCP service account keys; pipeline tries to refresh keys on every run leading to immediate failure for jobs that do not have pre-existing persisted keys.
Broker component creates a single session tag by joining branch, commit, and feature flags; combined length now exceeds AWS STS limit causing AssumeRole to be denied by request validation.
Some teams have previously stored long-lived keys and continue to pass, but any job that attempts rotation or runs on a fresh runner fails immediately.
mitigation_timeline: 2026-03-10 14:00 - Short-term mitigation: disabled key-rotation step in legacy pipeline for affected projects to allow previously issued keys to remain valid while we implement fix. (approved by Security)

2026-03-11 10:30 - Implemented a guard in broker to truncate/hashed session tags to 80 chars for critical pipelines to avoid AssumeRole rejection (hotfix applied to infra-broker service, canary in us-east).

2026-03-12 09:00 - Coordinated with security to whitelist a small service account provisioning path for one morning-only run to rotate keys for teams with compromised long-lived keys (manual approval required).
resolution_notes: Hotfix: infra-broker now truncates and deterministically hashes concatenated metadata into a single session tag field capped at 96 chars for backward compatibility. Deployed 2026-03-11 10:30 and validated across 10 reproduced runs.
Policy coordination: Security agreed to a controlled one-time key rotation window and to add guidance to the org policy rollout doc about impact to legacy CI. (2026-03-12)

Roadmap: Create a migration task to convert legacy pipelines to short-lived OIDC provider tokens (owner: infra-auth team), target completion: 2026-06-30. Backfill runbooks for teams that must maintain legacy keys.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:45 - Priya Nair: Noted multiple failing runs reported by infra-team. Opening internal ticket to coordinate with Security and SRE.
2026-03-10 12:15 - Jenna Ortiz (Security): Org policy rollout was intentional to reduce key sprawl. We're open to scoped exemptions for critical pipelines but prefer short-term technical mitigations.
2026-03-10 13:40 - Elliot Morales: Reproduced locally and confirmed both GCP key creation and AWS STS tag issues. Working on a broker-side truncation patch now.
2026-03-11 10:45 - Elliot Morales: Hotfix deployed to infra-broker canary; initial test runs in us-east succeeded. Rolling to eu-west after monitoring.
2026-03-12 08:50 - Marco Li (Infra Owner): Requesting a list of pipelines still on legacy keys so we can schedule migration and request temporary key-rotation window where necessary.
2026-03-12 16:30 - Priya Nair: Collated list and shared with Marco and Security. Planning migration sprint starting 2026-03-25.
